original_summary: A sickly railway worker lives with his wife at a remote trackside watch-house and has one nearby colleague. The colleague becomes bitter after repeated unfair treatment by railway officials, including a humiliating assault, and returns from seeking justice exhausted and desperate. He later tries to loosen a rail before a passenger train as an act of revenge. The first worker cannot repair the track or reach his warning flag in time, so he wounds his own arm and uses a blood-soaked handkerchief to signal danger and save the train.
seed_elements: Two isolated neighboring workers: one compassionate and responsible, the other driven toward revenge by prolonged injustice.
A vulnerable community is placed in danger by one person’s desperate act of sabotage.
A moral crisis in which there is no time for an orderly or safe solution.
An improvised warning signal that requires the protagonist to make a painful personal sacrifice.
The emotional core: compassion and responsibility overcoming anger, humiliation, and despair.
discarded_elements: The names Semen Ivanov and Vasili.
The Russian railway setting and nineteenth-century social conditions.
Specific pay disputes, petty rules, and the vegetable-patch incident.
The exact officials, journey to the city, and assault details.
The protagonist’s wife as a developed subplot and other minor background details.
conversion_plan: Modernize the story to a remote railway, mountain road, or transit-maintenance setting, keeping the isolated workplace and imminent public danger. Use accessible third-person narration, with clear dialogue and brief explanations of the characters’ conflict. Aim for 1,200–1,800 words at an intermediate English-learning level, emphasizing vocabulary for work, fairness, danger, and decision-making.
